audience.question: Before anything else — how much detail do you want in this document?
audience.selected: Plain English throughout, explain every term (recommended for Alex and Aurora)

wave-word.question: Is wave the word, finally?
wave-word.selected: Yes — wave. Lock it and I will use it everywhere

wave-customer.question: Does the customer see this word too, or only we?
wave-customer.selected: The customer sees it as well — one word everywhere

chk-wave.question: Alex sells Keno Group three packages. Each one contains an analysis, a build, a validation and a training. What has he sold, in the new words?

scope-of-records.question: Do departments, roles and tools belong to one customer each, or are they a shared library?
scope-of-records.selected: Each customer has their own — Keno Group's warehouse is not Hogo's (recommended)

role-people.question: How do people get into a role?
role-people.selected: Pick from the contacts we already hold for that company (recommended)

role-multi.question: Can one person hold more than one role?

role-dept.question: Does a role sit in exactly one department?

tool-fields.question: What does a tool record carry?
selected: How often it is billed (monthly / yearly)

tool-cost-history.question: When a tool's price changes, what happens to the old price?
tool-cost-history.notes: not sure we need to trakc this.

tool-owner.question: Do we track tools we pay for as well, or only the customer's?
tool-owner.selected: Only the customer's — this is an audit of their spend (recommended)

audit-rate-home.question: Where does the customer's staff hourly cost live?
audit-rate-home.selected: Its own new rate card, per customer — separate from both existing ones (recommended)

audit-rate-level.question: Is that hourly cost set on the role, the person, or the department?
audit-rate-level.selected: On the role — “a supervisor costs €38” (recommended, matches Aurora's description)

rate-visible.question: Can the customer see these staff costs in their portal?
rate-visible.selected: Yes — it is their own payroll, nothing secret about it

rate-currency.question: Currency — how do we handle it?
rate-currency.selected: One currency per customer, set once on the account (recommended)

chk-rate.question: Alex is auditing Keno Group. Their warehouse supervisor is paid about €38 an hour. Which of the three rate cards does that number belong on?
chk-rate.selected: The new one — the customer's own staff cost

step-kind-list.question: “Manual, automation, AI” — is that list fixed, or should you be able to add to it?
step-kind-list.selected: An editable dropdown, like ticket types are today (recommended)

step-status.question: Aurora's design shows steps in different colours — she said “we have the colours to play with status, but I do not know how we will use that yet.” What should the colour mean?
step-status.selected: Whether it has changed since the audit: original, changed, removed

step-cost-live.question: If a role's hourly cost is corrected later, should every step's cost move with it?
step-cost-live.selected: Yes — it is always worked out fresh (recommended)

step-tools.question: Can one step name more than one tool?
step-tools.selected: Just one (recommended — keeps the picture readable)

step-who.question: “Who does it” — a role, a named person, or either?
step-who.selected: A role (recommended — people change, the job does not)

step-frequency.question: How often a step runs — per what?
step-frequency.selected: Per month (recommended — what we already store)

build-method.question: How do you add a step?
build-method.selected: A form: name it, and pick what it comes after (recommended — Aurora's description)

decision-record.question: Is a decision (the diamond) a kind of step, or a different thing?
decision-record.selected: A kind of step, with its own kind value (recommended — one table, one picture)

decision-cost.question: Does a decision take time and cost money?
decision-cost.selected: Yes — deciding is work, and often the slowest part

branch-count.question: How many ways can a decision split?
branch-count.selected: Any number, each with its own label

branch-rejoin.question: Can two branches come back together into one step?
branch-rejoin.selected: Yes — real processes rejoin all the time

chk-decision.question: Looking at the picture above — how many steps does that process contain?
chk-decision.selected: Four, if a decision counts as a step

revision-model.question: Confirming the change: do we replace process versions with dated step history?
revision-model.selected: Yes — dated step history, versions go away (this is what the call agreed)

revision-date.question: When a step changes, who decides the date?
revision-date.selected: You type it — an audit records what was true last March, not today (recommended)

revision-future.question: Can a change be dated in the future — “this becomes automated on 1 September”?
revision-future.selected: Yes — that is a plan, and the map should hold it

removed-default.question: A step that was removed — does it show in today's view?

date-control.question: How do you pick the date you are looking at?

what-triggers.question: What makes a change get recorded?
what-triggers.selected: Only someone editing the step by hand (recommended for round one)

chk-timetravel.question: A step was removed on 15 August. You set the date on the process to 1 August. Do you see that step?
chk-timetravel.selected: Yes, as it was — it had not been removed yet on 1 August

baseline-def.section: What a saving is measured from
baseline-def.question: With versions gone, what does “as it was” mean?
baseline-def.selected: Each step's own earliest record — whenever we first wrote it down (recommended)

baseline-new-step.section: What a saving is measured from
baseline-new-step.question: A step that did not exist at the start and was added later — how does it count?
baseline-new-step.selected: It is a cost: new time we added, shown as a negative saving

baseline-slower.section: What a saving is measured from
baseline-slower.question: A step now takes longer than it did. Show it?
baseline-slower.selected: Yes — show it as a negative, it keeps the whole number honest (recommended)

savings-scope.section: What a saving is measured from
savings-scope.question: Should the savings number cover removed steps?
savings-scope.selected: Yes — eliminating a step is the biggest kind of saving there is (recommended)

tool-savings.section: What a saving is measured from
tool-savings.question: We drop a €300-a-month tool. Where does that show up?
tool-savings.selected: Alongside the hours, as money saved — a second figure next to the time (recommended)

chk-savings.section: What a saving is measured from
chk-savings.question: A customer opens their portal and sees “we have saved you 54 hours a month”. Under our rules, what must appear with that number?
chk-savings.selected: A sentence saying the times are agreed estimates and the subtraction is arithmetic

wave-shape.question: How should a wave be built?
wave-shape.selected: Its own record, and a sprint says which wave it belongs to (recommended)

wave-fields.question: What does a wave carry?
selected: A reference number like sprints have
The customer it was sold to
wave-fields.notes: strta and end date are calculated from sprints

wave-price.question: Where does the price live?
wave-price.selected: On the wave — that is what was sold (recommended)

wave-required.question: Must every sprint belong to a wave?
wave-required.selected: No — plenty of work is just a sprint (recommended)

wave-portal.question: Do customers see waves in their portal?
wave-portal.selected: Yes, but only the name and dates, never the price

portal-maps.question: Should a customer be able to open their own process maps in the portal?
portal-maps.selected: Yes, read-only — it is a map of their business and it makes the savings believable

portal-detail.question: If they can see a map, how much of it?
portal-detail.selected: Everything we see except our own numbers

portal-tools.question: Can a customer see the tools list and what those tools cost them?
portal-tools.selected: Yes — it is their own spend

portal-timetravel.question: Does the customer get the date slider too?
portal-timetravel.selected: Yes — “here is your business in June, here it is now” is the whole pitch

chk-portal.question: Which of these can a customer never see in their portal, no matter what anyone switches on?
chk-portal.selected: What our own hour costs us, and our margin

separate-app.question: Still happy with that?
separate-app.selected: Yes — one app (recommended, and much less work)

story-link.question: Confirm that stays out of this round?
story-link.selected: Out, but leave room in the design so it is easy to add

cut-order.question: If only part of this lands by the 25th, what matters most? Tick everything that must be in the first cut.
selected: Departments, roles, people and tools — the records themselves
Steps carrying kind, who, tool and cost

flowchart-first.question: The flowchart itself — how finished does it need to be on day one?
flowchart-first.selected: It must be editable on the picture from the start

alex-ready.question: What does Alex actually need in front of him for the first real audit?
alex-ready.selected: Not sure — explain the trade-off in chat
alex-ready.notes: enter the data, no need to show anything yet.

migration-risk.question: On the 25th we start moving data across. What worries you most about that?
selected: Old records arriving wrong and nobody noticing
Something that works in the old system missing in the new one
The team having to learn it during a live week

stop-using.question: Honest question: what would make you quietly stop using this module and go back to a spreadsheet?
selected: The picture not being good enough to show a customer
Not trusting the numbers it produces
stop-using.notes: fyi we dont' fillt his live, we fill it in using ai to extract from a call transcript.

missing.question: What is missing entirely? Something you expected to be asked about and were not.
